chunks: Faḍālah narrated from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Ghaylān, who attributed it to Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) saying:

There is no eye that wells up with tears out of fear of Allah but that He makes it forbidden to the Fire. If its tears flow upon the cheeks of its owner, neither gloom nor disgrace will cover his face. There is nothing but that it has a measure, except tears; for verily a single drop of it can extinguish seas of fire. If a man were to weep among his nation and a teardrop fell from him, they would all be shown mercy due to his weeping.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of weeping out of fear of God in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In the tradition of *al-Zuhd*, this hadith highlights the transformative power of *khishyah* (awe/fear of God), where tears serve as a spiritual shield against the humiliation of the grave and the fire of the Hereafter. Scholars note the unique metric of tears—having no fixed limit (*illa la al-dimaa*)—signifying that even a single drop from a sincere heart can extinguish vast seas of fire, reflecting the boundless mercy of Allah. This concept underscores the practical Shia emphasis on emotional piety (*muraqabah*) as a means of attaining divine proximity and communal intercession.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 2.Faḍālah narrated from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Ghaylān who attributed it to Abū Jaʿfar (a) saying, “

There is no eye that is welled up with tears out of fear of Allah but that He makes it forbidden to the Fire. If its tears then flow upon the cheeks of its owner, neither gloom nor disgrace will cover his face. There is nothing but that it has a measure, except tears; for verily a single drop of it can extinguish seas of fire. If a man were to weep among his nation and a teardrop fell from him, they would all be shown mercy due to his weeping.”
